_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with refractory, moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis whose disease is not adequately controlled with other systemic drug products, including biologics, or when use of those therapies is inadvisable.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group, multicenter monotherapy study of abrocitinib 100 mg QD, 200 mg QD, and placebo for 12 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects aged 12 years and older with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 12: proportion achieving IGA of clear (0) or almost clear (1) with a reduction from baseline of ≥2 points, and proportion achieving EASI-75.
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0/1 responder: 42.8% (200 mg), 23.7% (100 mg) vs 7.9% placebo; EASI-75 responder: 62.7% (200 mg), 39.7% (100 mg) vs 11.8% placebo.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group, multicenter monotherapy study of abrocitinib 100 mg QD, 200 mg QD, and placebo for 12 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects aged 12 years and older with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 12: proportion achieving IGA of clear (0) or almost clear (1) with a reduction from baseline of ≥2 points, and proportion achieving EASI-75.
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0/1 responder: 38% (200 mg), 28% (100 mg) vs 9% placebo; EASI-75 responder: 61% (200 mg), 44% (100 mg) vs 10% placebo.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, parallel group, multicenter study of abrocitinib 100 mg and 200 mg QD and dupilumab 300 mg Q2W versus placebo in adults on background topical therapy.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults on background topical therapy with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 12: proportion achieving IGA 0/1 and proportion achieving EASI-75.
pivotal_trials.n: N=837 (abrocitinib 200 mg: 226; abrocitinib 100 mg: 238; dupilumab: 242; placebo: 131)
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0/1 responder: 47% (200 mg), 36% (100 mg), 36% (dupilumab) vs 14% placebo; EASI-75 responder: 68% (200 mg), 58% (100 mg), 58% (dupilumab) vs 27% placebo.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%) include nasopharyngitis (12.4% at 100 mg, 8.7% at 200 mg vs 7.9% placebo), nausea (6.0% at 100 mg, 14.5% at 200 mg vs 2.1% placebo), and headache (6.0% at 100 mg, 7.8% at 200 mg vs 3.5% placebo). Serious risks include serious/opportunistic infections (herpes simplex, herpes zoster, pneumonia), thrombosis, thrombocytopenia and lymphopenia.
target_moa: Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor; abrocitinib reversibly and selectively inhibits JAK1 by blocking the ATP binding site, and its two primary metabolites (M1 and M2) inhibit cytokines that transduce signals via JAK1-dependent pathways.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for Serious Infections, Mortality, Malignancy, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), and Thrombosis. Patients may be at increased risk for serious infections leading to hospitalization or death (most frequent: herpes simplex, herpes zoster, pneumonia); higher rates of all-cause mortality, malignancies, MACE, and thrombosis were observed with JAK inhibitors.

rems.type: REMS is not proposed for this application; labeling and pharmacovigilance activities are considered adequate to convey the risks.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee was not convened for this product.

basis.text: The application was designated Priority review.

summary.text: Abrocitinib (CIBINQO) was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA and received Priority review; it was approved based on three pivotal Phase 3 trials with a boxed warning, without accelerated approval or a REMS, and no advisory committee was convened.

requirement.text: PMR 4217-3: Conduct a prospective observational study to assess the long-term safety of abrocitinib in U.S. adult patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, comparing incidence of adverse events of special interest against reference rates from patients treated with dupilumab or other chronic systemic treatments.

citations.quote: 4217-3 Conduct a prospective observational study (analyses conducted in patient cohorts enrolled prospectively and followed actively in accordance with a written protocol) to assess the long-term safety of abrocitinib treatment in U.S. adult patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis.

requirement.text: PMR 4217-4: Conduct or participate in a relevant Pregnancy Exposure Registry, a prospective registry-based observational cohort study comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to abrocitinib during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.

citations.quote: 4217-4 Conduct or participate in a relevant Pregnancy Exposure Registry, a prospective, registry based observational exposure cohort study that compare the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to abrocitinib during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: PMR 4217-5: Conduct an additional pregnancy study using a different design from the Pregnancy Exposure Registry to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, small for gestational age, and preterm birth in women exposed to abrocitinib during pregnancy versus an unexposed control population.

citations.quote: 4217-5 Conduct an additional pregnancy study that uses a different design from the Pregnancy Exposure Registry (for example a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data or a case control study) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, and small for gestational age and preterm birth in women exposed to abrocitinib during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: PMC 4217-6: Conduct a drug-drug interaction trial in healthy subjects using clinical dose of oral abrocitinib and gastric acid reducing agents (e.g., esomeprazole).
